summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted for a recurrent stage 4 sacral pressure ulcer and underwent successful sacral debridement with V-Y re-advancement flap coverage. He tolerated the procedure well, with stable postoperative course, adequate pain control, and gradual advancement to oral intake. He was transitioned from IV cefazolin to oral cefadroxil for antibiotic therapy. Despite fevers and a positive urine culture for Morganella morganii, he declined nephrostomy tube change during admission, though strongly advised to follow up with urology. He was discharged home with services, provided detailed wound and drain care instructions, and advised to use an air mattress and avoid pressure on the surgical site. Follow-up was arranged with plastic surgery, urology, and primary care, including imaging for a known lung nodule.
